title: What is the maximum number of non-convex components for degree d polynomials

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in complex analysis: What is the maximum number of non-convex components for degree d polynomials.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 2 irreducible axioms remain (complex analysis counterexamples). 0 sorries. S7 (2026-06-09): repaired pre-existing Mathlib v4.26.0 breakage in closedBall_isConvex (convex_closedBall is now ∀⦃x⦄, x∈s → StarConvex ℝ x s, not direct Convex API); added goodmanPolynomial_natDegree=4 and refereePolynomial_natDegree=6 via compute_degree!; dropped unused (a≠0) from pommerenkePolynomial_degree; theoremCount 11→13. Docker 2712 jobs clean.
builtItems: Proved pommerenkePolynomial_degree: deg(X^k(X-a)) = k+1 (S7: unused a≠0 hypothesis dropped — holds for every a∈ℂ including 0)
Proved goodmanPolynomial_degree_pos: degree > 0 (S7: simplified to rw [goodmanPolynomial_natDegree]; omega)
nonconvex_exists_degree_ge_4: proved trivially (maxNonConvexComponents d = d by definition, so d ≥ 4 → d ≥ 1)
lemniscate_isClosed: proved via isClosed_le + fun_prop (continuous preimage of closed set)

S7: Repaired closedBall_isConvex — Mathlib v4.26.0 broke .smul_add_smul_mem_of_nonneg_of_le dot notation on convex_closedBall result. New proof applies Convex_def directly: (convex_closedBall center r) hz hw (by linarith) ht0 (by ring).
insights: pommerenkePolynomial_degree provable via natDegree_mul + natDegree_pow (proof works for all a∈ℂ since X_sub_C_ne_zero holds even when a=0)
Monic for product polynomials via Monic.mul and monic_X_pow_add_C/monic_X_sub_C

compute_degree! (from Mathlib.Tactic.ComputeDegree) discharges exact natDegree facts for explicit polynomials — strictly stronger than simp+omega and replaces an indirect Monic.natDegree_pos eval-based contradiction approach

Mathlib v4.26.0 API change: Convex is now defined as ∀⦃x⦄, x∈s → StarConvex ℝ x s; old .smul_add_smul_mem_of_nonneg_of_le dot notation no longer resolves on the Convex predicate. Apply Convex directly as a 5-arg function: hconv hz hw (0≤a) (0≤b) (a+b=1).
nonconvex_exists_degree_ge_4 was trivially provable: maxNonConvexComponents is defined as d (placeholder), making the axiom just d ≥ 1 when d ≥ 4
lemniscate_isClosed: {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ c} is closed because z ↦ ‖f.eval z‖ is continuous and Iic c is closed
Both axioms (grunskyConjecture_false, goodman_counterexample) are independent — goodman_counterexample provides one c value but grunskyConjecture_false requires arbitrarily small c
nextSteps: maxNonConvexComponents def is currently a placeholder (= d). An honest definition would be supremum over deg-d polynomials of non-convex component counts — but that requires connected-component machinery on ℂ that doesn't yet exist in the file. Goodman's open question remains: pin down maxNonConvexComponents d exactly for small d.

Both remaining axioms require numerical/geometric verification of explicit lemniscate components (Goodman c=5^(3/2)/4, Pommerenke z^k(z-a)). Not tractable without computational complex analysis infrastructure in Mathlib.
